name: Class XI half-yearly: mixed paper

groups.note: A stock and flow question with a clock fault behind it: an unconfirmed firm estimate is an unsupported conclusion.
An interpretation question: a claim, its evidence, and the limit that bounds it.
An intermittent fault, so one clearing proves nothing until it is confirmed.
A group report whose parts do not join unless the hand-over is checked.
A clean stock and flow question with no hidden fault: confirming or hedging it wastes the time.

note: The first Class XI paper (SCHOOL_AND_PROGRESSION.md, Time economy): a 90-minute paper of eighteen five-minute units, five question groups worth twenty marks each, sat in the half-yearly window of the 2042-43 calendar. Its five questions are cases the four classroom structures already teach (two model, one each of explain, investigate and coordinate), so the examination re-asks what the classroom practised. A prepared character clears and confirms every group; an unprepared one must triage.
